gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the three makers' noise, distortion and output figures on one line and says that the Yamaha CD-S303's Pure Direct mode switches off the optical and coaxial outputs that are its main hardware edge over the optical-only Denon DCD-600NE, nor that Denon's own manual (12 W, 4.3 kg) and US product page (13 W, 4.0 kg) disagree with each other.
standout_why: Compared against Yamaha's CD-S303 specs page and manual (blocked for me, but they are Yamaha's own documents so they almost certainly carry the Pure Direct wording), the two Crutchfield compare pages (blocked, but Crutchfield normally tabulates S/N, outputs and headphone jack), Denon's web manual, Onkyo's product page and the insideouthomereviews round-up (opened: no S/N, THD or power figures at all, and it only flags the Denon weight conflict). The side-by-side S/N, THD, standby draw and Pure Direct caveat are only partly present in any single rival page; nothing I could open reports the Denon 12 W vs 13 W conflict.
decides: On the makers' own numbers the Denon leads on S/N (112 dB) and dynamic range (101 dB) but has no coaxial output; the Onkyo is the only one with a headphone jack and is the cheapest; the Yamaha is the only one with USB playback but loses both digital outputs whenever Pure Direct is on. For a shopper feeding an external DAC the Yamaha's advantage is conditional, which confirms the Onkyo as the practical pick and the Denon as the analog-only pick.
